answer: Each registered identity must hold a distinct hardware-root credential and lock a 400-unit bond in a shared vault for 20 epochs. Faking N identities therefore locks 400N units at once, and any proven duplicate forfeits the full bond plus a 25% penalty. Splitting one credential across copies raises marginal cost per identity and flags the shared vault, so independent jurors slash every linked bond through the registry bridge, leaving no cheap island of unbacked identities.
